title: ai-governance-watch source list
description: Schema for sources/literature-watch.yaml — the single source-of-truth URL list the watch pipeline crawls. Every watched URL must sit on the domain allowlist (Appendix E hardening).

version.description: Schema version. Bump only on a breaking shape change.

paused.description: Global maintenance switch. When true the routine runs in dry-run mode and produces logs only, no PRs.

user_agent.description: User-Agent sent on every fetch. Must identify the project and a contact (Appendix E).

cadence.description: Crawl cadence. The routine batches all due sources into one run.

adapter.description: Which adapter fetches and extracts this target.

allowlisted_url.description: HTTPS URL on the domain allowlist. Adding a new domain is a deliberate, reviewed schema change.

note.description: Optional human note on what this target covers.

watch_hint.description: What a fingerprint of this URL cannot see, and which page to check by hand when it stays silent: a successor that appears under a new identifier or URL (a revised NIST framework, a new ISO edition, a project that moves on), a chart that only renders in a browser, a host that refuses automated clients. The library's quelle_hinweis mechanic (2026-09-04). Required when the source declares successor_risk.

check_interval_days.description: Optional per-target override of the source cadence, in days. Shorten it for targets with successor risk or an announced consultation; the routine treats the target as due when this many days have passed since its last observation.

target_kind.description: What the target is, which decides what a change means. document: the source text itself (a change is a version bump or corrigendum). landing_page: the publisher's page about the source (a change is an announcement to read). news_feed: a list of new items — press releases, publications, news — whose NEW entries are compared against the page's Recent Changes, not fingerprinted as a whole (lesson of 2026-09-05: six developments lived only on news pages). legal_search: an EUR-Lex/registry view that lists acts based on or amending the source — the only way to see a delegated or implementing act that carries its own number (lesson of 2026-09-21: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1755 was missed by every landing-page watch).

id.description: Stable machine id. Used in branch names, labels, lock-free PR search, and the reference frontmatter.

title.description: Full title of the standard or body of work.

reference_file.description: The memory-mirror/ file this source maintains. Exactly one per source.

enabled.description: If false, the source is scoped but not yet crawled (planned state).

state.description: Rollout state, mirrors the README source-coverage table.

license.description: Human-readable license/reuse status of the source content (e.g. 'U.S. Government work — public domain', 'CC BY-NC-SA 4.0', 'ISO copyright — proprietary').

reproduction.description: Reproduction policy tier the library applies to this source. Governs how much of the source may be reproduced on a public page (vs. paraphrased in our own words).

successor_risk.description: True when a successor of this source would appear under a new identifier or URL, so that a fingerprint on the current URL would never fire (a framework under revision, a draft with a project page, a treaty chart behind a browser-only app). Every target of such a source carries a watch_hint, and the routine never reports the source as 'unchanged' without naming the hand-check.
